findings.reason: The protected solution is a concise, conventional greedy prefix-feasibility implementation. Its best, mask, bit, prefixes, candidate, and prefix names expose the algorithm directly, and no material change would improve its interview quality.

Metadata consistently identifies public LeetCode problem 421 and its Python findMaximumXOR surface. The Reference now preserves the source's i <= j contract, both examples in order, the first explanation, both constraints, and the permitted self-pair that makes a singleton result zero.

The immutable native source remains tied to verified submission 2064764912. Apart from the required Solution method adapter and List annotation, it is structurally identical to the app-local source: both build the mask from bit 30 downward, form the same prefix set and tentative candidate, perform the same partner lookup, and update the same best value.

The 64-, 192-, and 512-value tiers span 8x and keep the fixed 31-pass prefix scan distinct from pair enumeration. The current source passes all 11 executions at 1.00x the protected reference runtime; a correct pairwise control passes every output but fails only the runtime verdict at 7.83x.

The Approach exactly derives the most-significant-bit greedy, proves prefix feasibility through the unique candidate ^ p partner, gives an induction argument for retaining accepted higher bits, and states O(n) time with O(n) prefix-set space under the fixed 31-bit contract.

The hash-bound public Reference preserves the complete XOR objective, valid position relation, two source examples and first explanation, both source constraints, and the absence of source visuals or tables.
